summary: Introduces a collection of common data types for use with the YANG data modeling language, so modules can share definitions. It was replaced by RFC 6991.

eli5.summary: When people write blueprints for devices, many need things like an IP address or a counter. This supplies shared definitions so everyone does not reinvent them. A newer version replaced it.

questions: what is a yang data type
what are common yang types for network configuration
how do yang types align with smiv2
subtitle: Building blocks for YANG data models that handle IP addresses, counters, and network management

tldr.problem: The YANG data modeling language used to configure network devices defines only basic built-in types. Developers need common types such as IP addresses, port numbers, counters, and timestamps, which forces each module to define these types independently.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6021 defines two YANG modules containing derived types: ietf-yang-types for general-purpose types like counters and dates, and ietf-inet-types for Internet-specific types like IP addresses, prefixes, and domain names. All types are carefully aligned with existing standards such as SMIv2.
tldr.outcome: Network device models can use these shared type definitions, ensuring consistency across modules and making specifications easier to read and implement. These types were later refined by RFC 6991.

today: RFC 6021 was a Standards Track document published in October 2010. It was obsoleted by RFC 6991, which expanded and refined the collection of common YANG data types.

sections.title: Shared Types for Network Data Models
sections.content:
The YANG language is used to model configuration and state data for network devices managed by the NETCONF protocol. YANG provides a small set of built-in data types such as string, integer, and boolean, and mechanisms to derive new types from these built-in types through restriction or extension.

However, many YANG modules need the same derived types for concepts like IP addresses, counters, timestamps, and port numbers. Before RFC 6021, each module would define these types independently, leading to duplication, inconsistency, and confusion. The RFC defines two reusable YANG modules that contain commonly needed derived types, allowing modules to reference shared definitions.

The two modules are ietf-yang-types, containing general-purpose derived types, and ietf-inet-types, containing types specific to Internet protocols. These types are carefully designed to match equivalent types in SMIv2 (the older SNMP Management Information Base standard), ensuring consistency between new YANG-based systems and legacy SNMP systems.
sections.eli5: YANG needs definitions for common things like IP addresses and counters. Instead of each specification writing its own definitions, there is a shared list everyone uses.

sections.title: Core YANG Data Types
sections.content:
The ietf-yang-types module defines general-purpose types including counters, gauges, and timestamps. A counter32 represents a non-negative integer that monotonically increases until it reaches 2^32-1, then wraps to zero. A counter64 type provides a larger range up to 2^64-1. These types are useful for counting packets, octets, or events that always increase (though they may wrap).

A gauge32 or gauge64 represents a value that can increase or decrease and stays within a defined range, useful for measuring things like current connections or queue depth. The timeticks type represents time in hundredths of a second and is typically used as a base for calculating other time values. The timestamp type records when a specific event occurred relative to a timeticks reference point.

The module also defines types for identifiers such as object-identifier, which represents an ASN.1 Object Identifier as a sequence of numeric sub-identifiers, and phys-address and mac-address types for hardware addresses represented as hexadecimal octets separated by colons.
sections.eli5: These types handle things that count up, things that go up and down, times and dates, and network addresses written as strings of numbers and letters.

sections.title: Internet-Specific Derived Types
sections.content:
The ietf-inet-types module provides types specific to Internet protocols and addresses. The ip-version type is an enumeration indicating whether the IP version is unknown, IPv4, or IPv6. The port-number type represents a 16-bit TCP or UDP port number (0 to 65535). The as-number type represents an Autonomous System number (a 32-bit value assigned by IANA to identify an autonomous system in BGP).

Address types include ipv4-address, which matches the dotted-decimal notation (e.g., 192.0.2.1), and ipv6-address, which matches full, mixed, or compressed notation. Both address types support an optional zone index (preceded by a percent sign) to disambiguate link-local addresses on multi-interface systems. The ip-address type is a union that accepts either an IPv4 or IPv6 address, automatically detecting which format is used.

Prefix types such as ipv4-prefix and ipv6-prefix represent IP addresses with a prefix length in CIDR notation (e.g., 192.0.2.0/24). The domain-name type matches DNS domain names according to RFC 952 and RFC 1034 recommendations. The host type accepts either an IP address or a domain name, and the uri type represents a Uniform Resource Identifier as defined in RFC 3986.
sections.eli5: These types handle IP addresses in both IPv4 and IPv6 format, port numbers, domain names, network prefixes, and the version and size of internet packets.

sections.title: Alignment with SMIv2 Standards
sections.content:
The RFC carefully aligns the YANG derived types with equivalent types in SMIv2 (Structure of Management Information Version 2), which is the standard for SNMP Management Information Bases (MIBs). This alignment helps ensure interoperability between systems that use YANG-based configuration and legacy systems that use SNMP-based management. Where a YANG type is equivalent to an SMIv2 type, the RFC documents this equivalence.

For example, counter32 and counter64 have equivalent SMIv2 types with the same names. The gauge32 type is equivalent to Gauge32 from SNMPv2-SMI. The zero-based-counter32 and zero-based-counter64 types have defined starting values of zero and are equivalent to SMIv2 types from RMON2-MIB and HCNUM-TC respectively.

Some YANG types, such as object-identifier with arbitrary sub-identifier length, are supersets of their SMIv2 equivalents (which are limited to 128 sub-identifiers). The RFC includes a mapping table showing all YANG types and their SMIv2 equivalents or noting when no equivalent exists.
sections.eli5: These definitions match what the older SNMP standard uses, so new systems can work with old systems without translation.

sections.title: Reusability and Module Registration
sections.content:
Network device specifications and YANG modules can import these types and use them in their own data models. For example, a module modeling a router might use ipv4-address to define interface IP addresses, port-number to define protocol port bindings, and counter64 to define packet counts. By using the shared types, the module benefits from well-tested definitions and ensures that administrators using the model encounter familiar type semantics.

The IANA registry maintains entries for both modules with their namespace URIs, prefix abbreviations, and references to this RFC. The ietf-yang-types module uses namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-yang-types and the ietf-inet-types module uses urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-inet-types. These namespaces ensure that modules can safely import and reference these types without collisions with types defined in other modules.

Developers are encouraged to reuse these standard types rather than defining their own variants, which improves consistency across the ecosystem of network device models. Specialized domains may define additional derived types for their specific needs, but these core types provide the foundation that most network management models require.
sections.eli5: Device blueprints can use these shared definitions, so everyone is speaking the same language. The types are registered with official names so there is no confusion about which one to use.
